title: Hitchhiking from Tijuana to the North Pole: Thumbs Up Season 2 (Part 1/4)
summary: David Choe and Harry Kim restart Thumbs Up in Tijuana, return to Los Angeles through a border rail yard, briefly visit David's parents and head north toward Alaska by truck, hitchhiking and freight train. The episode holds its own strongest counterevidence: unsupervised testosterone injection is followed by sickness; a police officer and rail worker both warn them away from dangerous track behavior before they plan to board a moving train; and shelter seeking becomes admitted breaking and entering. The Fresno warehouse ends in an extended, speculative reading of explicit graffiti. The editorial layer preserves every idea and source-era term while keeping medical risk, coercive language, illegality, private family/driver identities, speculation and publisher speaker-label provenance separate from literal transcript text.

source_notes.claim: David Choe and Harry Kim are the primary travelers.
source_notes.assessment: VICE's manual captions repeatedly identify them. This is publisher annotation, not acoustic-model validation; enrollment still requires listening-verified clean windows.

source_notes.claim: Buying and self-injecting testosterone will make them juiced and able to keep running.
source_notes.assessment: FDA treats testosterone as prescription therapy for defined indications; unsupervised product, dose and injection safety are not established here. MedlinePlus warns that some testosterone injections require clinical observation and that higher-dose or non-directed use can cause serious effects.

source_notes.claim: The rail-yard worker warns that cars can move at any minute and not to cut between them.
source_notes.assessment: Federal Railroad Administration guidance says railroad trespass is dangerous and illegal, trains can come at any time and can overhang the track. The episode's warning is safety evidence, not an obstacle to work around.

speaker_policy.status: publisher labels retained; model-generated named turns withheld
speaker_policy.reason: The manual captions label David Choe, Harry Kim, Mr. Choe, Mrs. Choe, Arturo, a police-officer role and an unnamed male speaker. Retain those labels as source provenance only. Before enrollment, listen to non-overlapping speech and exclude Korean speech without a clear visible speaker, phone audio, music, narration over montage, quoted/imitation voices and offscreen ambiguity. Arturo, the officer and the anonymous worker are privacy-preserving negative controls, not people to unmask.
